chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave (bartered) with two slaves, and the slave with the slave and the dirhams. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with all of the animals, hand to hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bartering slaves or animals with currency in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of *riba al-fadl* (excess in exchange) does not apply to animals, allowing them to be bartered with slaves or currency provided the exchange is immediate (*yadan bi-yad*). This ruling distinguishes animals from staple commodities like wheat and barley, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the strict conditions of *sarf* (currency exchange) are not universally applicable to all goods. The emphasis on 'hand to hand' ensures the avoidance of *riba al-nasi'ah* (interest due to delay), a key principle in Islamic commercial law.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the slave (bartered) with two slaves, and the slave with the slave and the Dirhams. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with the (human or) the animals, all of them, hand to hand’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about exchanging one slave for two slaves and a slave for a slave and some dirhams. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful in the case of all animals if it (the deal) is simultaneous.’”
